Initial outdegree0 nodes enter sinks, else indegree0 enter sources. Preserve sink FIFO drain, then source FIFO drain, then if anything remains fallback. Each unprocessed endpoint degree tracks its remaining real nonself edges because processed marks prevent later decrements. A residual sink has no outgoing edge to an unprocessed node, so sink drain cannot create sources; residual sources analogously cannot create sinks. The >0 opposite-degree enqueue condition prevents a queued source from also becoming a sink and vice versa. Thus nodes are processed once, unprocessed count drops each step, and bounded loop ends. Sink marks are negative nextRight--, source/fallback marks positive nextLeft++.

Shift negative marks by n+1 to a total permutation1..n. Traverse actual nodes, snapshot node.ports then snapshot each current port.outgoing_edges. For each edge whose current source mark>target mark call approved reverse_edge(adapt_ports=True) then write graph.CYCLIC=true. Source swaps may make an edge visible later in the traversal; its new direction is increasing so it is not reversed again. Self-loops have equal marks and are never reversed. All retained nonself edges end forward in this total order, including antiparallel/parallel inputs, yielding an acyclic nonself orientation. CYCLIC false is not fabricated when no edge reverses.

At most8 original nodes/28 edges before dummy insertion: actual degrees/outflow in[-28,28], marks in[-8,8] before shift, resulting1..8, counts/indexes and priority0 sums are exact and far below signed32/IEEE53 limits. Every fallback consumes at least one mark0 node, so <=8 calls nextInt(k1..8). Private arrays are disposed and both FIFO queues reset after source returns; no original JSON/model field or geometry is changed.

Only for a connected simple directed ring n>=2, exactlyn nonself edges, every node1in1out, no extra/parallel/self edges, default priority/strategy: initial queues empty and all outflows0, so one fallback chooses v. For n>=3 its successor becomes a residual source and predecessor a sink. Sink drain follows the ring backwards through intermediate nodes; the remaining successor is source and drains last. For n=2 predecessor and successor are the same other node: actual port traversal can queue it as a source if the outgoing edge is visited first, or as a sink if the incoming edge is visited first; the strict residual-degree tests prevent a second queue insertion. It is processed exactly once and the shifted order is identical in both cases. Thus no second fallback occurs. The shifted order is v,successor,...,predecessor. Exactly the edge predecessor->v is reversed, leaving the Hamiltonian forward path plus v->predecessor shortcut (parallel two-edge path for n2). This is not a claim about arbitrary SCCs or any graph with an extra edge. Separate NS unit-tight-tree proof then forces n distinct ranks from that path; no same-layer spacing can be inferred merely from equal x for zero widths/between spacing.

guardProofs.proof: The admitted original graph is weakly connected ignoring self-loops; approved reverse_edge swaps endpoints but not the underlying undirected incidence. Default SelfLoopPreProcessor removes self-loops only and allocates no LNode. Thus the actual NS input still has one weak component, including an isolated singleton for loop-only input. Source connectedComponents assigns LNode IDs in current layerless order, repeats the actual port incoming-before-outgoing DFS, and initialize_4 creates one NNode per discovered original LNode. It then scans current source-node/port/outgoing order and creates one separate private NEdge for EVERY nonself LEdge, with no endpoint-keyed deduplication. Parallel edges and true REVERSED provenance survive; private connected-edge caches concatenate private incoming then outgoing, not original JSON edge order. PreviousLayeringNodeCounts stays null with one component.

Topological FIFO gives feasible integer ranks for unit delta on a DAG. Tight DFS rooted at the FIRST private node grows only to non-tree nodes or traverses already marked tree edges. If its node count<n, weak connectivity supplies a crossing edge; minimal nonnegative slack with the source orientation sign shifts the current tree, preserves feasibility, and makes at least one new crossing edge tight. At most n-1 node additions produce a connected tight spanning tree. Every true tree edge has directed rank difference1. No assumption that the first node is a source is permitted. Parallel edges do not invalidate the tree argument: source tightTreeDFS may choose only an edge to a previously non-tree node (or traverse an already-selected treeEdge). A second same-endpoint edge to the now-tree node is not inserted as an extra tree edge. Each parallel constraint is still checked separately by slack/topological indegree loops.

Compute actual postorder intervals and leaf-propagated cutvalues in source list order. For a tree edge, endpoint subtree intervals are nested: isInHead returns the component containing the directed target after deleting that edge. Preserve its literal condition. leaveEdge picks first insertion-ordered tree edge cut<-1e-10; enterEdge picks first strict-min slack crossing head->outside. Removing leave and adding enter retains a tree; shifting the outside by -slack makes enter tight while other tree edges keep difference1 and all directed edge spans stay>=1. Recompute postorder/cutvalues exactly. Degenerate exchanges still stop at the source iteration limit; do not continue to a textbook optimum. All parallel NEdges contribute their own unit weight to unknownCutvalues and cut sums. enterEdge still chooses the FIRST strict-min crossing edge in actual private edge order; an equal-span duplicate must not replace it. The tree is an identity set of selected NEdges, so deleting one edge and appending another preserves exact identity/order even for equal endpoint pairs.

A connected n-node tight tree with unit directed gaps has rank range<=n-1; a path between minimum and maximum visits every intervening integer rank, so normalized filling is nonempty in every layer. Source balance moves only equal-degree nodes and only to a strictly smaller filling. Such nodes either have incoming/outgoing neighbors or are the isolated singleton. minimalSpan literal ternary yields the true min incoming span and an outgoing bound no larger than the true min outgoing span (a non-min incoming edge may also reduce that bound). Thus its candidate ranks stay strictly between predecessors and successors. Since all candidate layers initially have count>=1, a moved-from layer had count>=2 and cannot be emptied. The singleton range is empty. Source balancing therefore retains feasible spans, no empty layer, and at most n layers. Do not rewrite the minimalSpan ternary into a different standard formula. Multiplicity changes indegree/outdegree equality and possible candidate ordering but not this feasibility proof: each predecessor/successor occurrence remains an independent unit-span constraint, the literal minimalSpan ternary still yields a conservative outgoing bound, and strict lower-filling moves cannot empty a layer. Cyclic original direction and REVERSED provenance are not read by the private solver.

This phase runs BEFORE dummy creation, so n<=8 and m<=28. The literal >=40 removeSubtrees condition is false. Initial ranks are integers0..7. During at most7 feasible-tree growth shifts a loose range recurrence Rnext<=2R+1 bounds transient ranges below1024. After the tight tree exists its range is<=7; at most84 exchanges shift one cut by a crossing slack whose magnitude is<=6, so all temporary ranks have magnitude well below4096. Cutvalue sums are bounded integral combinations of at most28 unit edges on an8-node tree (a conservative bound28*2^8=7168 suffices); filling/IDs/counters also stay far below2^31 and2^53.
